dedupe_keys.name: norway s national fm radio switch off and move to dab 2017

description: This policy case covers Norway's decision to become the first country to switch off national FM radio and rely on digital audio broadcasting (DAB+). The switch-off ran region by region from Nordland in January 2017 to Troms and Finnmark on 13 December 2017; many local stations stayed on FM. Reported results a year later were that 98 per cent of weekly listeners followed the change, comparing January 2017 with January 2018, while daily listening fell by about 10 percentage points at first and 7.7 points by April 2018. DAB+ reached 99.7 per cent of the population for NRK and 92.8 per cent for national commercial services, and the number of national stations rose from 5 on FM to 31. Critics pointed to consumer costs for new receivers, with no public subsidy, to the concentration of commercial capacity in two players, and to the loss of FM receivers in cars and homes as a channel for emergency information. The Norwegian Media Authority reported on the transition. Coverage: national, 2017 to 2018. Format and access: web pages and reports in Norwegian and English, free. Caveats: listening figures come from industry sources quoted in trade press; the Media Authority page could not be read on the day. Simulation uses: evaluation of technology transitions in broadcast networks, coverage and redundancy for public warning, and capacity planning for transmitter networks. Related records: the UK digital switchover of television is a comparable national transition.
